title_en: Russian strikes cut power to thousands in Ukraine as Kherson ceasefire ends
title_zh: 赫尔松停火结束后，俄罗斯空袭导致乌克兰数千人断电
summary: A rare humanitarian ceasefire allowed civilians to evacuate the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky.
summary_zh: 罕见的人道主义停火允许平民撤离俄罗斯占领的奥列什基市。
body_en: Image source, State Emergency Service of Ukraine
By Abdujalil Abdurasulov , Reporting from Kyiv and Ben Hatton
A rare humanitarian ceasefire in Ukraine's front-line Kherson region that allowed civilians to evacuate the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky has ended.
The localised ceasefire was due to end at 22:59 Ukrainian time (21:00 GMT) on Sunday. While the truce had held since it was implemented last week, fighting had continued elsewhere.
On Sunday evening, Ukraine's air alert system was apparently hacked, the country's air force said, warning of radiation over Kyiv - a reference to a possible nuclear attack.
The Air Force message read: "The Air Alarm application has probably been subjected to hostile interference. There is no radiation threat! Stay calm and follow our updates on our channel."

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia had struck energy infrastructure in four regions overnight on Saturday, leaving hundreds of thousands of homes without power. Some connections were restored on Sunday.
Another overnight strike killed two people, including a 13-year-old girl, in the Vinnytsia region, the State Emergency Service of Ukraine said.
Meanwhile, Ukraine hit a major missile fuel producer in Russia's Rostov region, which caused a fire and damaged four production facilities, Zelensky said.

In Ukraine, repair works to restore power continued throughout the day. Most customers in the Dnipropetrovsk region had their connections restored by early evening, but more than 60,000 were still without power, the governor said.

Because of regular attacks on energy infrastructure, emergency power cuts have been introduced across the country. Even in the capital Kyiv, electricity is cut off for most of the day, and water supplies are also disrupted.

Zelensky said in a social media post that the intensity of Russian strikes has been "extremely high" over the past week, adding that Russia was "trying to take maximum advantage of the shortage of ballistic missile interceptors".

He added that "every day" Ukraine communicated its need for Patriot missiles - the only effective weapon for downing Russia's deadly ballistic missiles - to the US, Europe and other partners. He thanked countries for their support so far and longer-term commitments, but called again for more immediate aid.
The limited pause in hostilities, which started on Tuesday, was brokered with the help of US First Lady Melania Trump and Pope Leo.

It was originally confined to the city of Oleshky, which has been occupied by Russia since the first days of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, and was expanded across the wider region of Kherson.
Oleshky had been trapped on one side by the Dnipro river and the other by Russian forces, with routes out mined and subject to drone attack.
Residents trapped there were suffering severe shortages of food, water and electricity, with many resorting to cooking garden weeds to survive.
The truce allowed for Oleskhy residents to evacuate if they wanted, and there were emotional scenes on Saturday of reunions between loved ones who hadn't seen eachother for years.

There are Ukrainian military positions just 5km (3.1 miles) from Oleshky, but evacuees had to travel through Russian-occupied territory to southern Russia, where they flew to Belarus, before finally being driven across Ukraine's northern border.
The oldest evacuee was 94 years old, while the youngest was one, according to Dmytro Lubinets, Ukraine's human rights ombudsman.

作者：Abdujalil Abdurasulov，基辅和 Ben Hatton 报道
乌克兰前线赫尔松地区罕见的人道主义停火已经结束，该停火允许平民撤离俄罗斯占领的奥列什基市。
局部停火将于乌克兰时间周日 22:59（格林尼治标准时间 21:00）结束。虽然休战自上周实施以来一直有效，但其他地方的战斗仍在继续。
乌克兰空军表示，周日晚上，乌克兰的空中警报系统显然遭到黑客攻击，并警告基辅上空有辐射——指的是可能发生的核袭击。
空军消息中写道：“空中警报应用程序可能受到敌意干扰。不存在辐射威胁！保持冷静并关注我们频道上的更新。”
乌克兰总统泽连斯基表示，俄罗斯周六夜间袭击了四个地区的能源基础设施，导致数十万家庭断电。周日恢复了一些连接。
乌克兰国家紧急服务部门表示，文尼察地区的另一场夜间袭击造成两人死亡，其中包括一名 13 岁女孩。
泽连斯基表示，与此同时，乌克兰袭击了俄罗斯罗斯托夫地区的一家主要导弹燃料生产商，引发火灾并损坏了四个生产设施。
在乌克兰，恢复供电的维修工作全天持续进行。州长表示，到傍晚时分，第聂伯罗彼得罗夫斯克地区的大多数用户已恢复供电，但仍有超过 6 万用户断电。
由于能源基础设施经常受到攻击，全国范围内实施了紧急断电。即使在首都基辅，一天中的大部分时间都断电，供水也中断。
泽连斯基在社交媒体帖子中表示，过去一周俄罗斯袭击的强度“极高”，并补充说俄罗斯“试图最大限度地利用弹道导弹拦截器短缺的优势”。
他补充说，乌克兰“每天”都会向美国、欧洲和其他合作伙伴传达其对爱国者导弹的需求，爱国者导弹是击落俄罗斯致命弹道导弹的唯一有效武器。他感谢各国迄今为止的支持和长期承诺，但再次呼吁立即提供援助。
周二开始的有限敌对行动是在美国第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普和教皇利奥的帮助下促成的。
它最初仅限于奥列什基市，自 2022 年 2 月俄罗斯全面入侵乌克兰的第一天起，该市就被俄罗斯占领，后来扩展到更广阔的赫尔松地区。
奥列什基的一侧被第聂伯河困住，另一侧则被俄罗斯军队困住，路线上布满了地雷，并受到无人机袭击。
被困在那里的居民严重缺乏食物、水和电力，许多人靠烹饪花园杂草来生存。
休战协议允许奥列斯基居民如果愿意的话可以撤离，周六也出现了多年不见的亲人团聚的激动人心的场面。
乌克兰军事阵地距离奥列什基仅 5 公里（3.1 英里），但撤离人员必须穿过俄罗斯占领的领土前往俄罗斯南部，从那里飞往白俄罗斯，最后被驱赶穿过乌克兰北部边境。
乌克兰人权监察员德米特罗·鲁比涅茨 (Dmytro Lubinets) 表示，撤离者中年龄最大的是 94 岁，最年轻的只有 1 岁。

title_en: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill eight including child, hospitals say
title_zh: 医院称，以色列对加沙的袭击造成包括儿童在内的八人死亡
summary: Five officers from the Hamas-run police have been killed in Khan Younis and three people, including a child, killed in Gaza City, officials say.
summary_zh: 官员称，哈马斯控制的警察的五名警官在汗尤尼斯被杀，包括一名儿童在内的三人在加沙城被杀。
body_en: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill eight including child, hospitals say - BBC News
Middle East correspondent , Reporting from Jerusalem
Israeli strikes in Gaza have killed at least eight people, including a child, according to hospitals, despite a year-old ceasefire.
In Gaza City to the north, hospital officials said a missile attack hit a group of civilians next to Cairo School in the Al-Rimal neighbourhood, killing three people, including a four-year-old boy.

In the southern city of Khan Younis, the Hamas-run ministry of interior said a drone attack targeted a group of police officers in the Al-Mawasi area, killing five, as they were carrying out their routine duties.
The Israeli military said it had carried out two attacks on what it described as military operatives but has not yet provided evidence or further information.
Outside Gaza City's Shifa Hospital, video showed a crowd of men gathered to pray next to two body bags and the tiny body of the child, which was wrapped in a white towel.

"My son and his child were martyred. They were sitting in their tent, bothering no one, and nothing else was happening in the area when suddenly, a missile struck them, and they were martyred," Ali Oweis told AFP news agency. "There is no ceasefire; the war is ongoing, don't you see?"

At Nasser hospital in Khan Younis, women despaired as body bags lay on the floor, video showed. The interior ministry named the five police officers killed, who were between the ages of 23 and 53, and called the attack a "horrific massacre".
A ceasefire came into force in Gaza in October last year, but Israeli air strikes have continued almost every day.

Since then, 1,580 people have been killed, according to Gaza's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN. Israel says it is targeting Hamas, but often civilians are also killed.
Meanwhile, a peace plan for Gaza, brokered by the Trump administration, has stalled.
The ceasefire saw thousands of Palestinians held by Israel released in return for all of the 48 remaining hostages held in Gaza, and an agreement to end the war.
The conflict was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 taken hostage.
Since the war began, 74,594 people have been killed in Gaza, according to the territory's health ministry.

body_zh: 医院称以色列对加沙的袭击造成包括儿童在内的八人死亡 -_澳门赌博平台
中东记者，耶路撒冷报道
据医院称，尽管已经停火一年，但以色列对加沙的袭击已造成至少八人死亡，其中包括一名儿童。
在北部的加沙城，医院官员表示，一次导弹袭击袭击了 Al-Rimal 社区开罗学校附近的一群平民，造成三人死亡，其中包括一名四岁男孩。
在南部城市汗尤尼斯，哈马斯控制的内政部表示，一次无人机袭击了马瓦西地区的一群警察，造成五人死亡，当时他们正在执行日常职责。
以色列军方表示，已对所谓的军事人员发动了两次袭击，但尚未提供证据或进一步信息。
在加沙市希法医院外，视频显示一群男子聚集在两个裹尸袋和用白色毛巾包裹着的孩子的小尸体旁边祈祷。
阿里·欧维斯告诉法新社：“我的儿子和他的孩子都殉难了。他们坐在帐篷里，没有打扰任何人，该地区也没有发生任何其他事情，突然，一枚导弹击中了他们，他们就殉难了。” “没有停火；战争仍在继续，你明白吗？”
视频显示，在汗尤尼斯的纳赛尔医院，尸体袋躺在地板上，妇女们感到绝望。内政部点名了五名遇难警察的名字，他们的年龄在23岁至53岁之间，并称这次袭击是一场“可怕的屠杀”。
加沙停火于去年10月生效，但以色列的空袭几乎每天都在持续。
据加沙哈马斯管理的卫生部称，自那以后已有 1,580 人被杀，联合国认为该数字是可靠的。以色列称其目标是哈马斯，但平民也经常被杀害。
与此同时，由特朗普政府斡旋的加沙和平计划陷入停滞。
停火后，以色列释放了数千名巴勒斯坦人，以换取加沙地带剩余的 48 名人质，并达成了结束战争的协议。
这场冲突是由哈马斯领导的 2023 年 10 月 7 日对以色列的袭击引发的，当时约 1,200 人被杀，251 人被扣为人质。
据该地区卫生部称，自战争开始以来，加沙已有 74,594 人丧生。

title_en: UN warns of security risks in Western Sahara as peacekeeping mission ends
title_zh: 维和任务结束后联合国警告西撒哈拉存在安全风险
summary: The mission, known as MINURSO, has been in place in the disputed region since a ceasefire in 1991.
summary_zh: 自 1991 年停火以来，这个名为 MINURSO 的特派团一直在争议地区开展工作。
body_en: Share UN warns of security risks in Western Sahara as peacekeeping mission ends on social media
United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has warned of potential escalation of hostilities in the disputed Western Sahara region after the expiry of a 35-year-long peacekeeping mission .

“The Secretary-General said he remains concerned about the security situation throughout the territory and the risk of hostilities escalating,” his spokesperson, Stephane Dujarric, said in a statement on Sunday.

Guterres also confirmed the end of the peacekeeping mission on Sunday, after the UN Security Council (UNSC) failed to renew its mandate on Friday.
He urged all concerned “to exercise maximum restraint and to refrain from actions that could further increase tensions or undermine regional stability”.
November 1 marked the start of the “liquidation phase” of the peacekeeping mission, with assets transported back to troop-contributing countries, Guterres said.
The UN established the Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO) in 1991 to monitor a ceasefire and prepare a referendum on the territory’s future.
Morocco has considered Western Sahara its territory since 1975, when Spain withdrew from the desert region in northwest Africa, roughly the size of Britain.
The Polisario Front, an Algeria-backed movement acting on behalf of the Indigenous Sahrawi people, seeks to establish an independent state called the Sahrawi Republic.

At the UNSC on Friday, the US proposed a resolution to support the principle of self-determination in the Western Sahara. Washington’s draft would have extended the mission for a year, removed “referendum” from its name and made Morocco’s autonomy proposal the only basis for further talks.
Russia vetoed the resolution, despite support from 11 of the 15 UNSC members, including fellow permanent members France and the United Kingdom.
The council then defeated a competing Russian resolution, leaving the mission to expire without a new mandate.

“While MINURSO’s peacekeeping operations have concluded, the United Nations stands ready to continue supporting efforts to advance dialogue and pursue a peaceful resolution of the conflict,” Guterres said on Sunday.
Morocco’s royal palace said the fact the mission was not renewed was a “significant development” in withdrawing the Western Sahara issue from the UNSC’s consideration.
On Saturday, Algeria’s Foreign Ministry, however, expressed “deep regret” over the non-renewal, blaming the “excessive bias” of the US towards Morocco’s position.
The Polisario Front said in a statement that it was “concerned at the deadlock in the Security Council meeting”.
Speaking after Friday’s vote, US Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz said it was truly unfortunate that in 2026, the veto was used to “preserve the letter R [in the Mission’s name] for referendum”.
body_zh: 联合国在社交媒体上警告维和任务结束后西撒哈拉存在安全风险
联合国秘书长安东尼奥·古特雷斯警告称，在长达 35 年的维和任务结束后，有争议的西撒哈拉地区的敌对行动可能会升级。
“秘书长表示，他仍然对整个领土的安全局势和敌对行动升级的风险感到担忧，”他的发言人斯蒂芬·杜雅里克在周日的一份声明中表示。

list 3 of 3 为什么摩洛哥庆祝联合国西撒哈拉问题决议的失败？
在联合国安理会（UNSC）周五未能延长其任务授权后，古特雷斯周日还确认了维和任务的结束。
他敦促有关各方“保持最大限度的克制，避免采取可能进一步加剧紧张局势或破坏地区稳定的行动”。
古特雷斯表示，11月1日标志着维和特派团“清理结束阶段”的开始，资产将运回部队派遣国。
联合国于 1991 年成立了西撒哈拉全民投票特派团 (MINURSO)，以监督停火并准备就该领土的未来举行全民投票。
自1975年西班牙撤出非洲西北部沙漠地区以来，摩洛哥一直将西撒哈拉视为其领土，该地区的面积与英国差不多。
波利萨里奥阵线是阿尔及利亚支持的代表撒哈拉土著人民的运动，旨在建立一个名为撒哈拉共和国的独立国家。
周五，美国在联合国安理会提出一项支持西撒哈拉自决原则的决议。华盛顿的草案将把任务延长一年，从名称中删除“公投”，并将摩洛哥的自治提案作为进一步谈判的唯一基础。
尽管联合国安理会 15 个成员国中的 11 个成员国（包括常任理事国法国和英国）支持该决议，但俄罗斯否决了该决议。
随后，该委员会否决了俄罗斯的一项竞争决议，使该任务在没有新任务的情况下到期。
古特雷斯周日表示：“虽然西撒特派团的维和行动已经结束，但联合国随时准备继续支持推动对话和和平解决冲突的努力。”
摩洛哥王宫表示，不再延长任务期限是联合国安理会考虑撤回西撒哈拉问题的“重大进展”。
然而，阿尔及利亚外交部周六对不续约表示“深切遗憾”，指责美国对摩洛哥的立场“过度偏见”。
波利萨里奥阵线在一份声明中表示，“对安理会会议陷入僵局感到担忧”。
美国驻联合国大使迈克·沃尔兹在周五投票后发表讲话时表示，非常不幸的是，2026年，否决权被用来“保留[代表团名称中的]字母R以供公投”。

title_en: Kherson braces for return of war as localised Russia-Ukraine truce ends
title_zh: 随着俄罗斯和乌克兰局部停战结束，赫尔松为战争回归做好准备
summary: Moscow and Kyiv continue strikes elsewhere, but no reported violations in Kherson region during the six-day ceasefire.
summary_zh: 莫斯科和基辅继续在其他地方进行罢工，但在为期六天的停火期间，赫尔松地区没有任何违规行为的报道。
body_en: Share Kherson braces for return of war as localised Russia-Ukraine truce ends on social media
The longest multi-day truce between Russia and Ukraine, limited to Ukraine’s eastern Kherson region, has come to an end with no violations reported by either side, but also no sign of an extension.
The truce, which ended on Sunday night, allowed hundreds of besieged residents of the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky to be evacuated in a rare joint operation between Kyiv and Moscow.

Russian strikes elsewhere in Ukraine on Sunday left hundreds of thousands of households without power, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. In Russia, meanwhile, authorities reported major ⁠damage to an industrial site following Ukrainian drone attacks on the Nizhny Novgorod region.

The six-day localised ceasefire in the front-line Oleshky and the surrounding area was reached after mediation efforts by United States First Lady Melania Trump and with the involvement of Pope Leo XIV. It was set to expire at 10:59pm Ukraine time (20:59 GMT).

On Sunday, Ukraine’s military said it evacuated 167 more people from threatened areas of the southern Kherson region, including 22 children and 21 people with limited mobility requiring special assistance.

“Units of civil-military cooperation of the ‘South’ group of forces, in cooperation with representatives of local authorities, evacuated 167 civilians to safer points in the Kherson region,” Ukraine’s General Staff wrote on Telegram.

An estimated 2,000 civilians were in Oleshky when the temporary truce took hold. They were offered the choice to evacuate to Kyiv-controlled territory of Ukraine or territory occupied by Russia, or to remain in the city with replenished food and medical supplies.

“The ceasefire across Oleshky and the surrounding Kherson region has provided residents with the freedom to move, access to food, clean water, medicine, plus a renewed sense of dignity without the constant threat of attack,” Melania Trump said on social media. “Let Oleshky become the starting point for lasting peace.”

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov, quoted by Russian news agencies, said Moscow had a positive view of how the operation was conducted in Oleshky, as well as of the coordination between the two countries’ human rights commissioners.
A Ukrainian official, however, told the AFP news agency that Russia reportedly refused an offer to extend the ceasefire after Kyiv’s Foreign Ministry proposed it.

Since Russia launched a full-scale invasion of its neighbour in February 2022, Moscow’s forces have occupied most of the eastern Ukrainian regions of Donetsk and Luhansk, as well as the majority of territory in Ukraine’s southern Kherson and Zaporizhia regions.
Kherson Governor Oleksandr Prokudin urged residents to be vigilant as the expiry of the ceasefire neared on Sunday.

“I also strongly urge you not to visit the so-called ‘red zones’ – areas and settlements near the Dnipro [River],” Prokudin wrote on Telegram. “The intensity of Russian strikes there remains high, and the threat to life is extremely high.”
Residents in Kherson city, one of the remaining areas of the region still controlled by Ukraine, remained calm, despite knowing the quiet of the localised ceasefire would soon end.
“Don’t be afraid, keep holding on,” Oleksandr Knyha, head of the Mykola Kulish Kherson Regional Academic Music and Drama Theater, told the audience as he opened a concert.

乌克兰总统泽连斯基表示，俄罗斯周日对乌克兰其他地区发动的袭击导致数十万户家庭断电。与此同时，俄罗斯当局报告称，乌克兰无人机袭击下诺夫哥罗德地区后，一处工业场地遭到严重破坏。
经过美国第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普的调解和教皇利奥十四世的参与，奥列什基前线及周边地区达成了为期六天的局部停火。它原定于乌克兰时间晚上 10:59（格林尼治标准时间 20:59）到期。
周日，乌克兰军方表示，已从赫尔松南部地区受威胁地区疏散了另外 167 人，其中包括 22 名儿童和 21 名行动不便、需要特别援助的人。
乌克兰总参谋部在 Telegram 上写道：“‘南方’部队的军民合作单位与地方当局代表合作，将 167 名平民疏散到赫尔松地区的安全地点。”
临时休战生效时，估计有 2,000 名平民在奥列什基。他们可以选择撤离到乌克兰基辅控制的领土或俄罗斯占领的领土，或者留在该市并补充食品和医疗用品。
梅拉尼娅·特朗普在社交媒体上表示：“奥列什基和周边赫尔松地区的停火为居民提供了行动自由、获得食物、清洁水和药品的机会，并在没有持续攻击威胁的情况下重新获得了尊严感。” “让奥列什基成为持久和平的起点。”
俄罗斯新闻机构援引克里姆林宫发言人德米特里·佩斯科夫的话说，莫斯科对奥列什基行动的进行方式以及两国人权专员之间的协调持积极看法。
然而，一名乌克兰官员告诉法新社，据报道，在基辅外交部提出延长停火协议后，俄罗斯拒绝了这一提议。
自2022年2月俄罗斯对其邻国发动全面入侵以来，莫斯科军队已经占领了乌克兰东部顿涅茨克和卢甘斯克地区的大部分地区，以及乌克兰南部赫尔松和扎波罗热地区的大部分领土。
周日停火即将到期，赫尔松州州长亚历山大·普罗库丁（Oleksandr Prokudin）敦促居民保持警惕。
普罗库丁在 Telegram 上写道：“我还强烈敦促你们不要访问所谓的‘红区’——第聂伯罗河附近的地区和定居点。” “俄罗斯在那里的袭击强度仍然很高，对生命的威胁极高。”
赫尔松市是该地区仍由乌克兰控制的剩余地区之一，尽管知道局部停火的平静很快就会结束，但居民仍然保持冷静。
“不要害怕，坚持下去，”米科拉·库利什·赫尔松地区学术音乐和戏剧剧院的负责人奥列克桑德·克尼哈 (Oleksandr Knyha) 在音乐会开幕时告诉观众。

title_en: France launches attempted murder investigation after petrol bomb thrown at police
title_zh: 法国向警察投掷汽油弹后启动谋杀未遂调查
summary: There were hundreds of arrests as protesters took to the streets in cities across France for the third weekend in a row.
summary_zh: 抗议者连续第三个周末走上法国各城市的街头，造成数百人被捕。
body_en: France launches attempted murder investigation after petrol bomb thrown at police - BBC News
Prosecutors in France have launched an attempted murder investigation after petrol bombs were thrown at police during unrest, French media reported.

An image of a police officer with his leg on fire during a clash with protesters in Paris on Saturday has prompted outrage and follows weeks of street protests in France that have also seen demonstrators injured.
The officer, who suffered burns to his ankle and minor injures to his hand, told French newspaper Le Figaro it was a "particularly sophisticated" incendiary device.
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said throwing a molotov cocktail at a police line was "what I call a murder attempt", adding officers were working to find the perpetrators.

Hundreds of thousands of people demonstrated across France in largely peaceful protests on Saturday, the latest in a series of youth-led protests that began in late September demanding action on the high cost of living and poor public services, especially schools.
Following previous clashes and looting, thousands of police officers were deployed across the country over the weekend, and officers fired tear gas at demonstrators in some cities.
There were more than 770 arrests on Saturday, roughly half as many as the previous week's protests, the French interior ministry said.
But police said no one had been arrested for the attack caught on camera that set a police officer on fire, AFP reported.

The officer - part of the National Gendarmerie, a national law enforcement force that is technically part of the military but under the control of the interior ministry - said his unit "suddenly found ourselves facing several hundred hostile, well equipped adversaries".
Speaking to French newspaper Le Figaro, he said police were yet to identify the liquid used but that the incendiary device "had a far greater burning capacity than a standard Molotov cocktail".
"We faced hostile individuals who are not protesters," he said. "These adversaries are there with the intent to harm those who represent the state."

Fourteen other officers sustained wounds ranging from minor to serious, he said, adding some were struck by paving stones. The unit was supposed to be on leave but had been urgently recalled to police the weekend protests, he said.

French protest organisers, the Gilets Jaunes, or Yellow Vests, have said dozens of protesters have been seriously injured during recent demonstrations across the country, with many hurt by "grenades".

France suspended the use of one type of stun grenade while policing student protests in early October after a 15-year-old's hand was blown off, but French newspaper Le Monde has reported that police have continued to use a different model in subsequent protests.

Protests also took place in Germany and Italy over the weekend , as mainly youth-led protests continue across parts of Europe, with varying demands but broadly linked to a focus on cost-of-living issues and public services.
body_zh: 法国向警察投掷汽油弹后启动谋杀未遂调查 -_澳门赌博平台
据法国媒体报道，法国检察官在骚乱期间向警察投掷汽油弹后启动了谋杀未遂调查。
周六，一名警察在巴黎与抗议者发生冲突时腿部着火的照片引发了愤怒，此前法国持续数周的街头抗议活动也造成示威者受伤。
这名警官脚踝被烧伤，手部受轻伤，他告诉法国报纸《费加罗报》，这是一个“特别复杂”的燃烧装置。
内政部长洛朗·努涅斯表示，向警戒线投掷燃烧瓶是“我所说的谋杀企图”，并补充说警察正在努力寻找肇事者。
周六，数十万人在法国各地举行了基本上和平的抗议活动，这是九月下旬开始的一系列青年主导的抗议活动中的最新一次，要求对高昂的生活成本和糟糕的公共服务（尤其是学校）采取行动。
继之前的冲突和抢劫之后，周末在全国各地部署了数千名警察，并在一些城市向示威者发射了催泪瓦斯。
法国内政部表示，周六有 770 多人被捕，大约是前一周抗议活动人数的一半。
但据法新社报道，警方表示，没有人因摄像机拍摄到的导致一名警察着火的袭击事件而被捕。
这名军官是国家宪兵队的一部分，国家宪兵队是一支国家执法部队，严格来说是军队的一部分，但受内政部控制。他说，他的部队“突然发现自己面临着数百名敌对、装备精良的对手”。
他在接受法国《费加罗报》采访时表示，警方尚未确定所使用的液体，但该燃烧装置“的燃烧能力比标准燃烧瓶的燃烧能力大得多”。
“我们面对的是不是抗议者的敌对人士，”他说。 “这些对手的目的是伤害那些代表国家的人。”
他说，另外 14 名警官受伤程度不等，其中一些是被铺路石击中的。他说，该部队本来应该休假，但在周末的抗议活动中被紧急召回以供警方处理。
法国抗议组织者“黄背心”表示，在最近全国各地的示威活动中，数十名抗议者受重伤，其中许多人是被“手榴弹”炸伤的。
10月初，一名15岁学生的手被炸飞后，法国在维持治安学生抗议活动时暂停使用一种类型的眩晕手榴弹，但法国报纸《世界报》报道称，警方在随后的抗议活动中继续使用另一种型号的眩晕手榴弹。
周末德国和意大利也发生了抗议活动，欧洲部分地区主要由年轻人领导的抗议活动仍在继续，抗议活动的诉求各不相同，但大体上都集中在生活成本问题和公共服务上。

title_en: Ukraine air raid app apparently hacked as users receive false radiation threat, Air Force says
title_zh: 空军称，乌克兰空袭应用程序显然遭到黑客攻击，用户收到虚假辐射威胁
summary: Authorities say there is no threat and have advised the public to stay calm and follow official channels for information.
summary_zh: 当局表示不存在威胁​​，并建议公众保持冷静并通过官方渠道获取信息。
body_en: Ukraine air raid app apparently hacked as users receive false radiation alert, Air Force says - BBC News
Ukraine's air raid alert app was apparently hacked on Sunday and for a short time said the capital Kyiv was subject to a radiation threat, the Ukrainian Air Force has said.
The Air Force message on Telegram read: "The Air Alarm application has probably been subjected to hostile interference. There is no radiation threat! Stay calm and follow our updates on our channel."

The Ukrainian Central Intelligence Agency said on Telegram that there had been a failure in the app, and urged people to use other sources of information to clarify the situation regarding the threat of air strikes.
The messages, in Ukrainian, started at approximately 22:47 (20:47 GMT), with the first reading: "Radiation threat. Radiation threat declared in Kyiv."
The next alert, written in Russian, came at 22:48, which read: "Hi! There will be a nuclear alert across Ukraine. Don't worry, it's Oreshnik flying".
A third alert, at 22:49, again in Ukrainian, said "Chemical threat. There is a threat of a chemical attack on Kyiv. Don't go outside."
At 22:49, a fourth alert stated there was a "Street fighting threat. Street fighting is taking place in Kyiv. Don't go outside."
A series of all clear messages were then delivered to users' phones, which were connected to each of the previous alerts, individually declaring each threat clear.

In a separate post, the Ukrainian Central Intelligence Agency said that due to the Air Alert application, the Radiation Hazard signal was played on loudspeaker devices in the Lviv region, and added there was no threat of radiation hazard.
It advised the public to turn on notifications on your smartphone, pay attention to sirens, and to only read official sources.
The governor of Vinnytsia oblast, Natalya Zabolotna said there had been a cyberattack on the Air Alert app and posted a warning on Telegram not to click on the link in the message.
The Air Alert app is supported by the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine, and informs users instantly about the beginning and end of defence alerts.
body_zh: 空军称，乌克兰空袭应用程序显然遭到黑客攻击，用户收到虚假辐射警报 - BBC 新闻
乌克兰空军表示，乌克兰的空袭警报应用程序显然于周日遭到黑客攻击，并在短时间内表示首都基辅受到辐射威胁。
空军在 Telegram 上发布的消息是：“空中警报应用程序可能受到了敌意干扰。不存在辐射威胁！保持冷静并关注我们频道上的更新。”
乌克兰中央情报局在 Telegram 上表示，该应用程序出现故障，并敦促人们使用其他信息来源来澄清有关空袭威胁的情况。
这些消息以乌克兰语于大约 22:47（格林威治标准时间 20:47）开始，第一条内容是：“辐射威胁。基辅宣布辐射威胁。”
下一次警报是用俄语写的，于 22 点 48 分发出，上面写着：“嗨！乌克兰各地将出现核警报。别担心，奥列什尼克在飞行”。
第三次警报于 22 点 49 分再次用乌克兰语发出：“化学威胁。基辅有化学袭击的威胁。不要外出。”
22点49分，第四条警报称存在“巷战威胁。基辅正在发生巷战。不要外出。”
然后，一系列完全明确的消息被发送到用户的手机，这些手机与之前的每个警报相连，单独声明每个威胁已清除。
乌克兰中央情报局在另一篇帖子中表示，由于空中警报应用程序，利沃夫地区的扬声器设备上播放了辐射危险信号，并补充说不存在辐射危险威胁。
它建议公众打开智能手机上的通知，注意警报器，并只阅读官方消息来源。
文尼察州州长 Natalya Zabolotna 表示，Air Alert 应用程序遭到网络攻击，并在 Telegram 上发布警告，不要点击消息中的链接。
空中警报应用程序由乌克兰数字化转型部支持，可立即通知用户防御警报的开始和结束。

title_en: UK was ‘vehement’ slavery reparations should not be on Commonwealth summit agenda
title_zh: 英国“激烈”奴隶制赔偿不应列入英联邦峰会议程
summary: British prime minister has now agreed to structured dialogue on reparatory justice but issue remains off formal Chogm agenda British officials reportedly insisted that discussions of reparations for slavery should not be on the agenda of the Commonwealth leade
summary_zh: 英国首相现已同意就赔偿性司法进行结构化对话，但该问题仍不在 Chogm 的正式议程中 英国官员报告
body_en: UK was ‘vehement’ slavery reparations should not be on Commonwealth summit agenda
British prime minister has now agreed to structured dialogue on reparatory justice but issue remains off formal Chogm agenda

British officials reportedly insisted that discussions of reparations for slavery should not be on the agenda of the Commonwealth leaders’ summit in Antigua and Barbuda – and even warned that Andy Burnham would not attend the meeting if the subject was formally included, according to a leading Caribbean political figure.

Ralph Gonsalves, a former prime minister of St Vincent and the Grenadines and a senior figure in the reparatory justice movement Repair Campaign, welcomed Britain’s decision to enter structured dialogue on reparations, but said the UK had come “kicking and screaming” to the conversation.
Currently, slavery reparations is not on the official agenda of the Commonwealth Heads of Government (Chogm) summit, which begins on Sunday.

Trade, climate resilience and finance, sustainable debt, democracy and investment in opportunities for young people are among the stated priorities for the 56-nation bloc spanning Africa, Asia, the Caribbean and the Americas, the Pacific and Europe.

“My understanding from informed circles is that Britain was vehement not to have the matter on the agenda. The British officials – and in that regard they were joined by the Canadian officials – were even raising the prospect that if it is on the agenda the prime minister of Britain wouldn’t go,” Gonsalves told the Guardian.

“They also started to circulate this untruth that India didn’t want it on the agenda, but that was not so at all. India was very supportive at the UN general assembly resolution on March 25th, 2026. So they were spreading this false word about India.”

Gonsalves said that the relentless campaign by Caribbean nations, amplified by a growing regional and global reparations movement, has propelled reparatory justice to the heart of the political conversation at the meeting.

“Because of what happened at the UN, because of what happened in Africa, what happened in the Caribbean, and all the work which is taking place in Britain itself too, inside of the British parliament, inside of the British Labour party, both in the Commons and the House of Lords, it is an issue which you can’t duck any more,” he said.

He added: “The danger of not putting it formally on the agenda is what we see happening now, that everybody who could have foreseen, whether or not it’s formally on the agenda, even the nature of how the discussions take place at the Commonwealth, and certainly in the retreats, it would have been raised.”

Gonsalves said while the actual structured dialoguewas unlikely to happen at Chogm, it was expected that when the leaders met in their private retreat, the format and details of the dialogue would be discussed.
He said: “The British government, they’re coming, kicking and screaming to the table of structured dialogue. But at least they’re coming.”

An FCDO spokesperson said: “We categorically reject this completely untrue accusation. The UK has approached this conversation in good faith, and we have at no point told any other Chogm member what should not be on an agenda.
“Our position on reparations is clear but this government respects the right of others to raise matters as they wish.”
‘We want a full apology for slavery’: Commonwealth at a crossroads as king heads to the Caribbean

Prof Sir Hilary Beckles, chair of the Caribbean Community (Caricom) Reparations Commission, had described the meeting as “the Chogm of reparations”, adding that reparatory justice was “the number one item” for the Caribbean as Commonwealth leaders gather in the region.
On Friday there was a historic shift in Britain’s position when the British prime minister went further than any of his predecessors by agreeing to structured dialogue and to consider an apology .

Though Caribbean governments and campaigners welcomed Burnham’s announcement, made in an op-ed for the Guardian, it was clear that agreeing on forms of reparations was still a priority for the region.
Guyana’s president, Irfaan Ali, welcomed Burnham’s statement and called for a Commonwealth subcommittee to work out the details of the dialogue over the next six to 12 months.
body_zh: 英国“激烈”奴隶制赔偿不应列入英联邦峰会议程
英国首相现已同意就赔偿性司法进行结构化对话，但该问题仍不在乔格姆的正式议程中
据报道，英国官员坚称，关于奴隶制赔偿的讨论不应列入安提瓜和巴布达英联邦领导人峰会的议程，据加勒比一位重要政治人物称，英国官员甚至警告称，如果该主题被正式纳入，安迪·伯纳姆将不会出席会议。
圣文森特和格林纳丁斯前总理、修复正义运动“修复运动”的高级人物拉尔夫·贡萨尔维斯对英国决定就赔偿问题进行结构化对话表示欢迎，但他表示，英国在对话中“又踢又叫”。
目前，奴隶制赔偿问题并未列入周日召开的英联邦政府首脑（Chogm）峰会的正式议程。
贸易、气候适应力和金融、可持续债务、民主和对年轻人机会的投资是跨越非洲、亚洲、加勒比地区、美洲、太平洋和欧洲的 56 个国家集团的既定优先事项。
“我从知情人士那里得到的理解是，英国极力不把此事列入议程。英国官员——在这方面加拿大官员也加入了他们的行列——甚至提出了这样的可能性：如果此事列入议程，英国首相就不会去，”贡萨尔维斯告诉《卫报》。
“他们还开始散布印度不希望将其列入议程的谎言，但事实并非如此。印度非常支持 2026 年 3 月 25 日的联合国大会决议。所以他们散布了有关印度的虚假消息。”
贡萨尔维斯表示，加勒比国家的不懈努力，加上日益壮大的区域和全球赔偿运动，将赔偿正义推向了会议政治对话的核心。
“由于联合国发生的事情，由于非洲发生的事情，加勒比海地区发生的事情，以及英国国内、英国议会内部、英国工党内部、下议院和上议院正在开展的所有工作，这是一个你不能再回避的问题，”他说。
他补充道：“不将其正式列入议程的危险就是我们现在所看到的情况，每个能够预见的人，无论它是否正式列入议程，甚至在英联邦，当然还有务虚会上如何进行讨论的性质，都会被提出。”
贡萨尔维斯表示，虽然实际的结构化对话不太可能在乔姆举行，但预计当领导人在私人静修中会面时，将讨论对话的形式和细节。
他说：“英国政府，他们来了，又踢又叫地来到结构化对话的桌子上。但至少他们来了。”
FCDO 发言人表示：“我们断然拒绝这一完全不实的指控。英国本着善意进行这次对话，我们从未告诉任何其他 Chogm 成员什么不应该列入议程。
“我们在赔偿问题上的立场很明确，但本届政府尊重其他人按照自己的意愿提出问题的权利。”
“我们希望为奴隶制道歉”：国王前往加勒比海，英联邦正处于十字路口
加勒比共同体（Caricom）赔偿委员会主席希拉里·贝克尔斯（Hilary Beckles）爵士教授将这次会议描述为“赔偿的乔格姆”，并补充说，当英联邦领导人聚集在该地区时，赔偿正义是加勒比地区的“头等大事”。
周五，英国的立场发生了历史性转变，英国首相比任何一位前任都走得更远，同意进行结构化对话并考虑道歉。
尽管加勒比各国政府和活动家对伯纳姆在《卫报》专栏中宣布的消息表示欢迎，但很明显，就赔偿形式达成一致仍然是该地区的首要任务。
圭亚那总统伊尔法安·阿里对伯纳姆的声明表示欢迎，并呼吁英联邦小组委员会在未来 6 至 12 个月内制定对话细节。

title_en: Russia's giant new radar in Kaliningrad raises alarm in NATO
title_zh: 俄罗斯在加里宁格勒的巨型新雷达向北约发出警报
summary: Russia is nearing completion of what experts think is a giant radar complex in Kaliningrad, capable of monitoring much of Europe. Experts warn the project could intensify the military standoff between Moscow and NATO.
summary_zh: 俄罗斯即将完成专家认为位于加里宁格勒的巨型雷达综合体，能够监视欧洲大部分地区。专家警告亲
body_en: The Kremlin is getting closer to opening its 'new eye' on Europe. Construction of a towering radar complex is almost complete in Russia's highly militarized exclave of Kaliningrad, according to reports.

From above, the three radiating arms of the sprawling facility – each more than 500 meters long – look like some sort of alien lifeform has left its mark on an otherwise undisturbed stretch of forested nature reserve. You could actually compare it to a landing platform or launch pad for Moscow's massive intelligence-gathering network.

While Russia has not confirmed it is building the structure, security expert Vaidotas Malinionis said the radar will be so big, it will be able to see beyond the earth's curvature. The retired commander from Lithuania told DW the over-the-horizon (OTH) radar network near Gvardeysk will have a surveillance range of about 3,000 kilometers, allowing Moscow to peer into almost every corner of Europe, as well as right across Ukraine .
The system would reportedly allow Russia to intercept satellite communications and detect aircraft movements and ballistic missiles.

"The goal and the purpose of this radar is observation of long-distance targets and early warning capabilities. We still don't know if it is operationally capable of doing that, but it is definitely being constructed right now," he added.

The British newspaper The Times reports that the systems are primarily intended for the detection and jamming of electronic signals – citing the Finnish-Polish space and defense technology company ICEYE.
"They would be able to use it in offensive operations, to get more information about specific targets," explained Malinionis.
"And if they were able to get an early warning about the movement of NATO troops, in the case of an invasion on NATO's eastern frontier, then they would gain more time for decision-making."

Speaking to DW from the shores of the Baltic Sea, Latvian geopolitical analyst Evija Djatkovica warned there is a significant downside for NATO to this old Soviet technology being revived when it comes to the increased use of new tech in the warfare of today.
"It will help Russia close existing loopholes in detecting low-flying objects, making the rapidly developing integration of drones into regional defense doctrines less effective," she claimed.
Russia ramps up drone war with new launch megabase

The Times report goes on to say that ICEYE sees Russia's expansion of its OTH radar system as proof that Kaliningrad is being developed into a hub for advanced military sensors and electronic warfare systems.
"The new radar signals an intensifying contest between Russia and NATO for military supremacy and control of the Kaliningrad region," Djatkovica underlined.

"This is a potentially dangerous situation, since further militarization on both sides could be expected and, at some point, a preemptive strike becomes an option to deny the other side an unacceptable advantage over the region,” she warned.

Russia has already alerted NATO it would be ready to resort to nuclear weapons if the Western alliance attempted to blockade Kaliningrad. The potential flashpoint and Russian outpost is situated on the Baltic Sea, wedged between NATO member states Poland and Lithuania – on the very doorstep of the alliance's eastern flank.
The exclave is only 200 kilometers from west to east and 100 kilometers from north to south. However, from what Malinionis asserted, Russia's smallest federal region or oblast packs a punch.

"According to some sources, they have the capability to deploy up to 100 nuclear warheads in Kaliningrad. And some sources say they have already started deploying some there – although that is yet to be confirmed," the former commander pointed out.

ICEYE claims to have discovered another large circular antenna complex some 50 kilometers west of Gvardeysk, near the city of Chernyakhovsk, according to the German daily Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung (FAZ). More than 20 signal and electronic warfare facilities are reportedly peppered throughout the Kaliningrad region.

Satellite images also reveal new shelters for fighter jets at the Kaliningrad-Chkalovsk military airfield, according to the FAZ report. Other images show launch pads at the mobile S-400 surface-to-air missile site in Baltiysk, meaning the systems could well be operational.

“该雷达的目标和目的是观察远距离目标和预警能力。我们仍然不知道它在操作上是否有能力做到这一点，但它现在肯定正在建造中，”他补充道。
英国《泰晤士报》援引芬兰-波兰太空与国防技术公司 ICEYE 的话说，这些系统主要用于检测和干扰电子信号。

拉脱维亚地缘政治分析师埃维贾·贾特科维卡(Evija Djatkovica)在波罗的海沿岸接受德国之声采访时警告称，在当今的战争中越来越多地使用新技术，这对北约来说是一个重大的不利因素。

title_en: Armed police start patrols in Sydney after Bondi Beach attack
title_zh: 邦迪海滩袭击事件后，武装警察开始在悉尼巡逻
summary: The new police unit is a security measure in response to last year's deadly shooting attack at a Hanukkah festival.
summary_zh: 新警察部队是针对去年光明节致命枪击事件而采取的安全措施。
body_en: Heavily-armed police officers have started patrolling Sydney's streets, as part of heightened security measures following last year's deadly shooting at Bondi Beach.
The Armed Response Command (ARC) will see specially trained officers in busy tourist areas carrying long-arm rifles – an unfamiliar sight for most residents.

New South Wales police say the officers will also patrol major events like sports matches and places of worship "to prevent, deter and rapidly respond to serious threats, including active armed offender incidents".
Fifteen people - including a 10-year-old girl – were killed in December when two gunmen opened fire on an event marking the Jewish festival of Hanukkah at the popular beach.
The attack was Australia's worst mass shooting in almost three decades and prompted sweeping gun law reforms and a crackdown on hate speech.
One resident told ABC news that the sight of armed police was "unnerving".
"They are just everywhere. Those guns are huge."
But another woman told the broadcaster that seeing police with weapons made her feel safe.
ARC is specifically designed to be "highly visible across Sydney, driving specialist vehicles and carrying rifles," New South Wales police said in a statement.
Its role "is built on a simple principle - preserving life," Detective Superintendent Andrew Evans said.
The shooting on 14 December put huge pressure on Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's government, with calls for immediate action on antisemitism.
Jewish communities have welcomed the new police operation, which will eventually consist of 250 officers, but others have called for safeguards to protect human rights.
"No Australian wants to see officers with military weapons on our streets, but the sight of body bags is far worse," Alex Ryvchin, co-CEO of Executive Council of Australian Jewry, said.

But Amnesty International Australia said it was concerned about the "militarisation of policing", and asked for assurances from the state government that ARC will not be used to suppress peaceful protests.
"Any expansion of police powers and capabilities must be accompanied by clear, publicly accessible rules, robust independent oversight and accountability," said the organisation's Andrew Witheford.
The New South Wales administration defended the new measures.

"Our world changed forever. That's just the truth of it, right across this country. And I said it at the time, we will never be the same again," the state's Police Minister Yasmin Catley told the ABC.
One of the alleged gunmen, Naveed Akram, has been charged with 78 offences including 15 counts of murder, 40 counts of attempted murder, and one count of committing a terrorist act.
His father, Sajid Akram, 50 - who was also armed and shot at the crowd on Bondi Beach - was killed by police at the scene.
A national tragedy 30 years ago united Australia. Why hasn't the Bondi shooting?
body_zh: 去年邦迪海滩发生致命枪击事件后，全副武装的警察开始在悉尼街道巡逻，这是加强安全措施的一部分。
武装反应司令部（ARC）将在繁忙的旅游区看到经过专门训练的军官携带长臂步枪——这对大多数居民来说是陌生的景象。
新南威尔士州警方表示，警察还将巡逻体育比赛和礼拜场所等重大活动，“以预防、威慑和快速应对严重威胁，包括武装犯罪事件”。
12 月，两名枪手向热门海滩举行的庆祝犹太光明节的活动开枪，造成 15 人死亡，其中包括一名 10 岁女孩。
这次袭击是澳大利亚近三十年来最严重的大规模枪击事件，并引发了全面的枪支法改革和对仇恨言论的打击。
一名居民告诉美国广播公司新闻，看到武装警察“令人不安”。
“它们无处不在。那些枪很大。”
但另一名妇女告诉广播公司，看到警察携带武器让她感到安全。
新南威尔士州警方在一份声明中表示，ARC经过专门设计，“驾驶特种车辆并携带步枪，在悉尼引人注目”。
侦探警司安德鲁·埃文斯说，它的作用“建立在一个简单的原则上——保护生命”。
12 月 14 日的枪击事件给安东尼·阿尔巴内塞总理的政府带来了巨大压力，人们呼吁立即对反犹太主义采取行动。
犹太社区对新的警察行动表示欢迎，该行动最终将由 250 名警官组成，但其他人则呼吁采取保障措施来保护人权。
澳大利亚犹太人执行委员会联合首席执行官亚历克斯·里夫钦 (Alex Ryvchin) 表示：“没有一个澳大利亚人希望在我们的街道上看到携带军事武器的警察，但看到裹尸袋的情况就更糟糕了。”
但澳大利亚国际特赦组织表示，它对“警务军事化”感到担忧，并要求州政府保证不会使用 ARC 来镇压和平抗议活动。
该组织的安德鲁·威瑟福德（Andrew Witheford）表示：“警察权力和能力的任何扩张都必须伴随着明确、公开的规则、强有力的独立监督和问责制。”
新南威尔士州政府为新措施进行了辩护。
“我们的世界永远改变了。这就是整个国家的事实。我当时就说过，我们再也不会一样了，”该州警察部长亚斯明·卡特利 (Yasmin Catley) 告诉美国广播公司 (ABC)。
其中一名被指控的枪手 Naveed Akram 被指控犯有 78 项罪名，其中包括 15 项谋杀罪、40 项谋杀未遂罪和一项实施恐怖行为罪。
他的父亲，50 岁的萨吉德·阿克拉姆 (Sajid Akram) 在邦迪海滩也持枪向人群开枪，在现场被警察击毙。
30 年前的一场全国性悲剧团结了澳大利亚。邦迪枪击事件为何没有发生？

title_en: University of Cambridge scientist among those who died in Spanish train crash
title_zh: 剑桥大学科学家在西班牙火车事故中丧生
summary: Marta Shahbazi was an "inspiring, talented and passionate scientist", says the laboratory where she worked.
summary_zh: 玛尔塔·沙巴齐 (Marta Shahbazi) 工作的实验室称，她是一位“鼓舞人心、才华横溢且充满热情的科学家”。
body_en: Image source, MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology
An award-winning University of Cambridge researcher died in the Spanish train disaster while on her way to collect a prize for scientific excellence.
Dr Marta Shahbazi was travelling to an awards ceremony on Wednesday when the train she was on crashed into another near Urda, south of Madrid, killing 69 people.

The mother of two was an affiliate associate professor leading a group of researchers at MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology (LMB) in Cambridge and had earned several awards for work on human embryos and cell biology.
In a statement, the LMB paid tribute to the "inspiring, talented and passionate scientist" and described her death as a "profound shock and a huge loss".
The expert in cell biology ran the Shahbazi Laboratory at the LMB, based on the Cambridge Biomedical Campus.

She had been announced as the winner of a Spanish Society for Developmental Biology award for her contributions to the study of early human development and was due to collect the award at a conference in El Rompido in Andalusia.

The LMB said: "As a wife and mother of two young children, Marta wrote eloquently about balancing her family and career, serving as a much-admired role model for a 'mother scientist', a term she used to describe herself.

"Marta was an inspiring, talented and passionate scientist whose research shed light on the earliest steps in the development of human embryos and how errors occur that lead to failed pregnancies," the LMB said.
The institute said her death was "a profound shock and a huge loss for LMB".
Her work had been recognised with "many awards and prizes", the laboratory added.
Shahbazi is listed on the University of Cambridge website as a principal investigator at its Stem Cell Institute (CSCI).
Institute director Prof Bertie Gottgens said its community was "shocked and deeply saddened" by her death.

"Marta led her primary research group at the MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology (LMB) alongside her roles as an affiliate principal investigator and affiliate assistant professor at the CSCI," he said.
"Across both institutes, she was highly respected for her pioneering research on early human development and valued for her collaborative spirit.
"Her creativity, passion, and generosity will be greatly missed."
The news of her death was first confirmed in a social media post , external by the CiMUS, based in Santiago de Compostela where Shahbazi's aunt works.
Shahbazi undertook her PhD at the Spanish National Cancer Research Centre, before joining the University of Cambridge as a post-doctoral fellow and then the LMB in 2020.
The crash in Spain happened when a state-operated Renfe high-speed train smashed into the back of a stationary train operated by the Iryo company.
body_zh: 图片来源，MRC 分子生物学实验室
剑桥大学一位获奖研究员在领取科学卓越奖的途中在西班牙火车灾难中丧生。
周三，玛塔·沙赫巴齐 (Marta Shahbazi) 博士在前往参加颁奖典礼的途中，所乘坐的火车在马德里南部乌尔达附近与另一列火车相撞，造成 69 人死亡。
这位两个孩子的母亲是剑桥 MRC 分子生物学实验室 (LMB) 的副教授，领导一组研究人员，并因在人类胚胎和细胞生物学方面的工作而获得多项奖项。
LMB 在一份声明中向这位“鼓舞人心、才华横溢、充满激情的科学家”致敬，并将她的去世描述为“深刻的震惊和巨大的损失”。
这位细胞生物学专家在位于剑桥生物医学园区的 LMB 管理着 Shahbazi 实验室。
由于她对早期人类发育研究的贡献，她被宣布为西班牙发育生物学学会奖的获得者，并将在安达卢西亚埃尔龙皮多举行的一次会议上领取该奖项。
LMB 表示：“作为一名妻子和两个孩子的母亲，玛塔雄辩地阐述了如何平衡家庭和事业，成为了备受推崇的‘科学家母亲’的榜样，她用这个词来形容自己。
LMB 表示：“玛塔是一位鼓舞人心、才华横溢且充满热情的科学家，她的研究揭示了人类胚胎发育的最早步骤以及导致怀孕失败的错误是如何发生的。”
该研究所表示，她的去世“对 LMB 来说是一个深刻的震惊和巨大的损失”。
该实验室补充说，她的工作获得了“许多奖项和奖品”。
Shahbazi 在剑桥大学网站上被列为其干细胞研究所 (CSCI) 的首席研究员。
研究所所长伯蒂·戈特根斯教授表示，其社区对她的去世感到“震惊和深切悲伤”。
“Marta 在 MRC 分子生物学实验室 (LMB) 领导她的主要研究小组，同时担任 CSCI 的附属首席研究员和附属助理教授，”他说。
“在这两个研究所，她因其对早期人类发展的开创性研究而受到高度尊重，并因其协作精神而受到重视。
“她的创造力、热情和慷慨将被人们深深怀念。”
她去世的消息首先在社交媒体帖子中得到证实，该帖子由 CiMUS 外部发布，该机构位于圣地亚哥德孔波斯特拉，Shahbazi 的姨妈在那里工作。
Shahbazi 在西班牙国家癌症研究中心获得博士学位，随后作为博士后研究员加入剑桥大学，并于 2020 年加入 LMB。
西班牙的事故发生时，一列国营Renfe高速列车撞上了Iryo公司运营的静止列车的后部。

body_en: The US-China trade war seems to have subsided – but the sense of calm is misleading | China
The US-China trade war seems to have subsided – but the sense of calm is misleading
A truce has cooled the trade conflict, but neither country has done anything to limit the outbreak of new hostilities

Donald Trump ’s trade wars have largely fallen off the headlines. Fears of new tariffs flare up from time to time when the US president goes off the rails – for instance, threatening to end US trade with countries with which it has a deficit unless the Federal Reserve cuts interest rates. But the sense that the world’s two largest economies are plowing ahead into an overt economic conflagration has taken a back seat to other, more salient fears, about Trump ending American democracy, AI killing us all and stuff like that.
The sense of calm is misleading. Under the radar, the world is marching toward an economic war of potentially epic proportions, one that, history suggests, could well spill over into the real thing.

The truce reached by Washington and Beijing last year in their escalating trade conflict, which has been extended until next January, lowered the heat between the two – putting an end to the escalation of tit-for-tat tariffs and opening a door to some as yet undefined future trade deal.

But neither China nor the US has done anything to establish the mutual assurances that could limit the outbreak of new hostilities. Rather, they are both focused on gaining the upper hand in what seems like an inevitable next round, in a standoff that both sides have defined as a national security priority, essential to ensure economic, technological and military supremacy.

The new arms race is different from those in the past. Rather than building weapons to blow each other up, China and the US are focusing on ensuring the resilience of the international supply chains on which they rely and figuring out how to constrain – and if push comes to shove, throttle – the supply chains essential to the economic and technological progress of their rival.
The survival of American democracy depends on taxing billionaires

The paired strategies go back at least to the Covid pandemic, when China’s Xi Jinping called on the nation to “tighten international production chains’ dependence on China, forming a powerful countermeasure and deterrent capability against foreigners who would artificially cut off supply [to China]”.

Early in the Biden administration, national security adviser Jake Sullivan articulated the American goals: to limit China’s access to a narrow set of advanced technologies with military applications without upending the global economic order. He described the strategy as building a “small yard” of forbidden tech surrounded by a “high fence” of trade and investment controls.

By now, the conflict has breached the bounds of these initial rationales. Restrictions on American tech exports, investments and technology transfers to China have proliferated over the last half decade. And they are hitting not only China’s military capabilities but slowing its technological progress writ large. And Trump’s wanton deployment of tariffs is not helping.

China, on the other hand, is becoming increasingly assertive, leveraging its overwhelming dominance over the supply of critical minerals that are essential to high-tech industries for civilian and military uses. Last year, it stunned the Trump administration by throttling exports of rare earths and magnets made from them to retaliate against US tariffs and efforts to restrict China’s access to high-end semiconductors and the lithography machines needed to make them.

It has relaxed some of these controls, but it maintains many other restrictions . While they have largely been imposed to retaliate against American actions, they have also been used to hit other countries for a variety of policies it dislikes. The stakes are high. The International Energy Agency has estimated that if China were to block the US’s and Europe’s access to rare earth magnets, it could cost their economies about $1.5tn per year.

Where does the supply chain war go from here? The Trump administration is pouring hundreds of millions into projects to mine and process rare earths and other critical minerals, hoping to close China’s lead. It is also doubling down on efforts to limit China’s access to frontier semiconductors and to bar it from buying the machinery needed to make them.

China, on the other hand, has announced a range of high-tech export restrictions , covering things such as artificial intelligence chips and solar power technology. Moreover, it has threatened to punish countries that work to reduce their dependence on its mineral inputs.

One hopes there is a path to a peaceful entente. This would probably require some shared understanding of what constitutes a legitimate national security risk that may warrant actions to block supply chains. Defining the “yard” is essential. Frustrations of standard commerce should not be dealt with on a wartime footing.

China will probably dominate renewable energy technologies, especially the solar power industry, into the foreseeable future. It may also dominate the electric vehicle industry. This might hurt in Brussels and Washington, but it’s not worth a war. China, on the other hand, will have to accept that its mercantilistic economic strategy is not tenable for the rest of the world. Its combination of massive export growth with zero import growth is not sustainable.

This might seem doable. And yet the odds that the world economy will remain at peace seem slim. One might recall the Axis powers’ efforts to seize territories as the League of Nations curtailed their access to raw materials in the early stages of the second world war. Or FDR’s blocking of sales of American scrap steel and oil to Japan, which likely contributed to Tokyo’s decision to attack Pearl Harbor. Today, American fighter jets, submarines and missiles use rare earth magnets. What would happen if China blocked access to these materials?

The moment is strange. It’s not that long ago that trade was proposed as perhaps the most powerful tool to deliver world peace, building positive-sum interdependence among nations. That’s over. Interdependence has become a vulnerability. As China and the United States fight over who will control the next generation of technology, trade has become a theater of war.
body_zh: 中美贸易战似乎已经平息——但这种平静感具有误导性 |中国
中美贸易战似乎已经平息——但这种平静的感觉具有误导性
休战已经冷却了贸易冲突，但两国都没有采取任何措施来限制新敌对行动的爆发
唐纳德·特朗普的贸易战基本上已经不再成为头条新闻。当美国总统出轨时，人们对新关税的担忧时不时就会出现——例如，威胁称除非美联储降息，否则美国将结束与有赤字国家的贸易。但世界上最大的两个经济体正在陷入一场公然的经济大火，这种感觉已经让位于其他更明显的担忧，比如特朗普结束美国民主、人工智能杀死我们所有人等等。
平静的感觉是误导性的。在人们的关注下，世界正在走向一场可能规模空前的经济战争，历史表明，这场经济战争很可能蔓延到真正的战争中。
去年，华盛顿和北京在不断升级的贸易冲突中达成休战协议，并已延长至明年一月，这降低了两国之间的紧张程度，结束了针锋相对的关税升级，并为一些尚未确定的未来贸易协议打开了大门。
但中国和美国都没有采取任何行动来建立可以限制新敌对行动爆发的相互保证。相反，他们都专注于在似乎不可避免的下一轮对峙中占据上风，双方都将这场对峙定义为国家安全优先事项，这对于确保经济、技术和军事霸权至关重要。
新的军备竞赛与以往不同。中国和美国不是制造武器来炸毁对方，而是专注于确保各自所依赖的国际供应链的弹性，并找出如何限制 — — 如果情况严重的话，会扼杀 — — 对对手的经济和技术进步至关重要的供应链。
美国民主的生存取决于对亿万富翁征税
这两种策略至少可以追溯到新冠疫情期间，当时中国习近平呼吁国家“收紧国际生产链对中国的依赖，对外国人人为断供（对华）形成强大的反制和威慑能力”。
在拜登执政初期，国家安全顾问杰克·沙利文阐明了美国的目标：在不颠覆全球经济秩序的情况下，限制中国获得少数具有军事用途的先进技术。他将该战略描述为建造一个禁止技术的“小院子”，周围环绕着贸易和投资管制的“高墙”。
到目前为止，冲突已经突破了这些最初理由的界限。过去五年来，美国对中国的技术出口、投资和技术转让的限制不断增加。它们不仅打击了中国的军事能力，而且明显减缓了其技术进步。特朗普肆意征收关税也无济于事。
另一方面，中国正变得越来越自信，利用其在关键矿产供应方面的压倒性主导地位，这些矿产对民用和军用高科技产业至关重要。去年，它限制了稀土和稀土磁体的出口，以报复美国的关税以及限制中国获得高端半导体及其制造所需的光刻机的努力，此举震惊了特朗普政府。
它放松了其中一些控制，但仍保留许多其他限制。虽然这些措施主要是为了报复美国的行动，但也被用来打击其他国家不喜欢的各种政策。赌注很高。国际能源署估计，如果中国阻止美国和欧洲获得稀土磁体，每年可能会给它们的经济造成约 1.5 万亿美元的损失。
供应链战将何去何从？特朗普政府正在向稀土和其他关键矿物开采和加工项目投入数亿美元，希望缩小中国的领先地位。它还加倍努力限制中国获得前沿半导体并禁止其购买制造这些半导体所需的机器。
另一方面，中国宣布了一系列高科技出口限制，涵盖人工智能芯片和太阳能技术等。此外，它还威胁要惩罚那些努力减少对其矿产投入依赖的国家。
人们希望有一条通往和平协约的道路。这可能需要对什么构成合法的国家安全风险有一些共同的理解，这可能需要采取行动阻止供应链。定义“院子”至关重要。标准商业的挫折不应该在战时的基础上处理。
在可预见的未来，中国可能会主导可再生能源技术，尤其是太阳能行业。它还可能主导电动汽车行业。这可能会伤害布鲁塞尔和华盛顿，但不值得发动战争。另一方面，中国将不得不承认其重商主义经济战略对于世界其他国家来说是站不住脚的。大规模出口增长与零进口增长的结合是不可持续的。
这似乎是可行的。然而世界经济保持和平的可能性似乎很小。人们可能还记得二战初期，随着国际联盟限制轴心国获取原材料的机会，轴心国努力夺取领土。或者罗斯福阻止向日本出售美国废钢和石油，这可能导致东京决定袭击珍珠港。如今，美国战斗机、潜艇和导弹都使用稀土磁铁。如果中国阻止获取这些材料会发生什么？
这一刻很奇怪。不久前，贸易被认为是实现世界和平、在国家间建立正和相互依存的最有力工具。就这样结束了。相互依赖已成为一种弱点。随着中国和美国争夺下一代技术的控制权，贸易已成为战场。

title_en: Shops looted as German cost-of-living protests turn violent
title_zh: 德国生活成本抗议演变成暴力，商店被洗劫
summary: The protests in cities across Germany - including Berlin, Hamburg and Frankfurt - came on the same day hundreds of thousands also protested in France.
summary_zh: 法兰克福警方表示，市中心发生了“暴力骚乱”，柏林、汉堡和科隆也有报道称发生骚乱。
body_en: Rioters looted shops in central Frankfurt late on Saturday as clashes erupted in German cities over the cost of living.

Besides Frankfurt - Germany's financial hub - there were incidents of violence in Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg, with police saying they used water cannon to disperse protesters who were targeting emergency workers with fireworks, stones and bottles.

Thousands joined largely peaceful demonstrations earlier in the day. They were organised by the campaign group Gen Z regelt - meaning "Gen Z takes charge" - to protest against underfunding in schools, the high cost of living, public spending cuts and military service.
The unrest in Germany follows similar youth-led mass protests in France, where more than 320,000 people also demonstrated on Saturday.

On Sunday, Germany's Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt told Bild newspaper that overnight police had prevented "violence like that seen in Paris" in recent weeks and called for "harsh punishments" for rioters and looters.
Overnight, a large section of Frankfurt's main shopping street was closed off by police. A police spokesperson said many arrests were made in the city.

Authorities in Frankfurt, Munich and Berlin reported as many as 18,000 protesters, roughly half of what the organisers had estimated on their website. German media say tens of thousands protested in German cities on Saturday.
Gen Z regelt spokesperson Lina Friedrich said the demonstrations were "to fight for peace and freedom, rather than for war and coercion".
She said: "What matters most to us is better support for the health and education systems. We are against compulsory military service and we are in favour of a fairer distribution of the burden."
Europe's youth is on the march - but does anything actually unite them?
On Saturday night Frankfurt police said "violent riots" were occurring in the city centre and that special police units had been deployed.
The windows of several shops had been smashed and molotov cocktails were thrown at emergency services, police said.
Officials said the windows of a gun shop were smashed and that they had seized two weapons after arresting a suspect. People also broke into other shops, stealing items like trainers.

Roman Poseck, interior minister of Hesse state, of which Frankfurt is the biggest city, said that "around 100 clearly identified left-wing extremists" had infiltrated the protest in the city. He added that it was "shameful" how the protests had ended.
"We all have those images from France in our minds - looting, burning houses, burning police vehicles, and attacks on police officers... France must not be held up as a model in this regard."
Police said the situation calmed down overnight into Sunday in the city.
Similar instances took place in other German cities, following largely peaceful demonstrations.
In Cologne, police said officers were attacked near the main train station, with bottles thrown and a bicycle launched.

Cologne's police chief Johannes Hermanns said it was "deeply saddening that young people who wanted to peacefully demonstrate for their future were infiltrated today by extremists who had nothing but violence in mind".
A smaller demonstration in the evening in Berlin - following larger protests in the day - resulted in 27 police officers being injured, and up to 56 people temporarily detained, Berlin police said.
body_zh: 周六晚间，随着德国各城市因生活成本问题爆发冲突，暴乱者抢劫了法兰克福市中心的商店。
除了德国金融中心法兰克福外，柏林、科隆和汉堡也发生了暴力事件，警方表示，他们使用高压水枪驱散抗议者，这些抗议者向急救人员投掷烟花、石块和瓶子。
当天早些时候，数千人参加了基本上和平的示威活动。这些活动是由运动团体 Gen Z regelt（意思是“Z 世代负责”）组织的，目的是抗议学校资金不足、生活成本高昂、公共开支削减和兵役。
德国发生骚乱之前，法国也发生了类似的青年领导的大规模抗议活动，周六也有超过 32 万人示威。
周日，德国内政部长亚历山大·多布林特 (Alexander Dobrindt) 对《图片报》表示，近几周来，警方连夜阻止了“巴黎发生的暴力事件”，并呼吁对骚乱者和抢劫者进行“严厉惩罚”。
一夜之间，法兰克福主要购物街的一大片区域被警方封锁。警方发言人表示，该市逮捕了许多人。
法兰克福、慕尼黑和柏林当局报告称抗议者人数多达 18,000 人，大约是组织者在其网站上估计人数的一半。
Gen Z regelt 发言人莉娜·弗里德里希 (Lina Friedrich) 表示，示威活动是“为了和平与自由而战，而不是为了战争和胁迫”。
她说：“对我们来说最重要的是更好地支持卫生和教育系统。我们反对义务兵役制，我们赞成更公平地分配负担。”
欧洲的年轻人正在前进——但有什么东西能够真正将他们团结起来呢？
周六晚上，法兰克福警方表示市中心发生“暴力骚乱”，并已部署特警部队。警方称，几家商店的窗户被砸碎，并向紧急服务部门投掷燃烧弹。
警方称，几家商店的窗户被砸碎，并向紧急服务部门投掷燃烧弹。
官员们表示，一家枪店的窗户被砸碎，他们在逮捕一名嫌疑人后缴获了两把武器。据当地媒体报道，人们还闯入其他商店，偷走运动鞋和其他物品。
黑森州（法兰克福是黑森州最大的城市）内政部长罗曼·波塞克（Roman Poseck）表示，“大约 100 名明确身份的左翼极端分子”已渗透到该市的抗议活动中。他补充说，抗议活动的结束方式是“可耻的”。
“我们脑海中都有来自法国的那些画面——抢劫、焚烧房屋、焚烧警车、袭击警察……法国在这方面绝不能成为榜样。”
警方表示，该市的局势到周日夜间已经平静下来。
德国其他城市也发生了类似事件，此前主要是和平示威。
在科隆，警方表示，警察在火车总站附近遭到袭击，有人投掷瓶子，还扔了一辆自行车。
科隆警察局长约翰内斯·赫尔曼斯表示，“令人深感悲痛的是，那些想要为自己的未来和平示威的年轻人今天却被只想着暴力的极端分子渗透”。
柏林警方表示，继当天规模较大的抗议活动之后，柏林晚上举行了一场规模较小的示威活动，导致 27 名警察受伤，多达 56 人被暂时拘留。

title_en: Democrat endorses Republican candidate in key Michigan Senate race as party spat erupts
title_zh: 民主党在密歇根州参议院关键竞选中支持共和党候选人，党内争端爆发
summary: The move by Haley Stevens, who lost out on the Democratic Senate nomination to Abdul El-Sayed, was called a "despicable betrayal" by one top Democrat.
summary_zh: 海莉·史蒂文斯(Haley Stevens)在民主党参议院提名中输给了阿卜杜勒·赛义德(Abdul El-Sayed)，他的举动被一位民主党高层称为“卑鄙的背叛”。
body_en: By Ana Faguy and Nada Tawfik , North America correspondent in Detroit, Michigan
A Democrat in Michigan has endorsed the Republican candidate in the state's crucial US Senate contest, as a spat with her own party's candidate Abdul El-Sayed escalated just days before the vote.
Haley Stevens, a sitting congresswoman who lost out on the Democratic Senate nomination to El-Sayed, made a surprise appearance alongside the Republican candidate Mike Rogers on Sunday.

"I don't belong in Abdul's campaign," she said in a video posted to X shortly after that appearance. "Who we are as Michiganders is not hate and is not what we are getting out from our Democratic nominee right now."
"That's why I am endorsing Mike Rogers," Stevens said.

The move stunned many of Stevens' fellow Democrats who condemned her decision to break from the party and switch her support just two days before the election, with one calling it a "despicable betrayal".
The public feud between Stevens, a centrist Democrat, and El-Sayed, who represents the party's left-wing, has boiled over in recent days.

Stevens called on El-Sayed to denounce a campaign advert from an outside liberal group that linked US support for Israel with high prices. El-Sayed criticised the advert and said he had nothing to do with its contents.

Stevens had been scheduled to appear at an event with El-Sayed on Sunday in an effort to display party unity, but he reportedly asked her not to come and she chose to attend a church service with his Republican opponent instead.

"This is a very close election, we all know that, but Abdul made clear that I was not welcome in his campaign, that he didn't need me there, that he didn't want me there," Stevens told reporters as she stood alongside Rogers outside the church.
When asked about Stevens' endorsement, El-Sayed told reporters he was focused on the problems Michiganders are facing.
"At the end of the day, I don't think about Haley Stevens," he said on Sunday. "None of this matters."
EXPLAINED: Why Trump's approval rating matters in the midterms
IN DEPTH: The Republicans walking a Trump tightrope

The Michigan Senate race is considered by analysts to be one of the tightest in Tuesday's midterm elections. It is one of a handful of battleground contests that will ultimately decide control of the Senate.

The seat is currently held by a retiring Democrat and the last time a Republican was elected to this Senate seat was in 1994. But in presidential elections, it is one of the crucial swing states - Michigan voted for Joe Biden in 2020 but Donald Trump in 2024.
Rogers welcomed Stevens' endorsement and said it showed "courage" during brief remarks with reporters.
President Donald Trump echoed that sentiment during a campaign rally in Iowa, calling her "very brave".
"I don't know Haley. I've never met Haley. But Haley said what few people were willing to say," Trump said. "I'd love her to join the Republican Party actually."

Many of Stevens' staff reportedly resigned immediately after her announcement, while the chair of the Democratic Party in Michigan said her decision "shows that she has abandoned everything she claims to care about".
body_zh: 作者：Ana Faguy 和 Nada Tawfik，驻密歇根州底特律的北美记者
密歇根州的一名民主党人在该州至关重要的美国参议院竞选中支持了共和党候选人，因为就在投票前几天，她与自己党派候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德的口角升级。
在民主党参议院提名中输给埃尔赛义德的现任国会女议员海莉·史蒂文斯 (Haley Stevens) 周日与共和党候选人迈克·罗杰斯 (Mike Rogers) 一起出人意料地亮相。
“我不属于阿卜杜勒的竞选活动，”在那次露面后不久，她在发布到 X 的视频中说道。 “作为密歇根人，我们并不是仇恨，也不是我们现在从民主党候选人那里得到的信息。”
“这就是我支持迈克·罗杰斯的原因，”史蒂文斯说。
此举震惊了史蒂文斯的许多民主党同僚，他们谴责她在选举前两天脱离党并改变支持的决定，其中一人称这是“卑鄙的背叛”。
中间派民主党人史蒂文斯和代表该党左翼的埃尔赛义德之间的公开争执最近几天已经白热化。
史蒂文斯呼吁埃尔赛义德谴责一个外部自由主义团体的竞选广告，该广告将美国对以色列的支持与高价格联系起来。埃尔-赛义德批评了这则广告，并表示他与广告内容无关。
史蒂文斯原定于周日与埃尔-赛义德一起出席一场活动，以展示党派团结，但据报道，史蒂文斯要求她不要来，而她选择与他的共和党对手一起参加教堂礼拜。
“我们都知道，这是一场非常接近的选举，但阿卜杜勒明确表示，我在他的竞选活动中不受欢迎，他不需要我在那里，他不希望我在那里，”史蒂文斯站在教堂外的罗杰斯旁边告诉记者。
当被问及史蒂文斯的支持时，埃尔-赛义德告诉记者，他关注的是密歇根人面临的问题。
“归根结底，我不会想到海莉·史蒂文斯，”他周日说道。 “这些都不重要。”
解释：为什么特朗普的支持率在中期选举中很重要
深入：共和党人在特朗普走钢丝
分析人士认为，密歇根州参议院竞选是周二中期选举中最激烈的竞选之一。这是最终决定参议院控制权的少数战场之一。
该席位目前由即将退休的民主党人担任，上一次由共和党人当选该参议院席位是在1994年。但在总统选举中，它是关键的摇摆州之一——密歇根州在2020年投票给了乔·拜登，但在2024年投票给了唐纳德·特朗普。
罗杰斯对史蒂文斯的认可表示欢迎，并表示在与记者的简短讲话中表现出了“勇气”。
唐纳德·特朗普总统在爱荷华州的一次竞选集会上呼应了这一观点，称她“非常勇敢”。
“我不认识海莉。我从未见过海莉。但海莉说了很少有人愿意说的话，”特朗普说。 “实际上我希望她加入共和党。”
据报道，史蒂文斯的许多工作人员在她宣布这一消息后立即辞职，而密歇根州民主党主席表示，她的决定“表明她已经放弃了她声称关心的一切”。

title_en: High-ranking US Democratic senator suffers stroke
title_zh: 美国民主党高级参议员中风
summary: Senator Chris Murphy, a fierce Trump critic who is not up for re-election in the midterms, is 'alert' after a stroke.
summary_zh: 参议员克里斯·墨菲 (Chris Murphy) 是一位激烈的特朗普批评者，他在中期选举中不打算连任，但在中风后变得“警觉”。

United States Senator Chris Murphy , a high-ranking Democratic legislator, has suffered a stroke but is “awake and alert”, his senior aide said.
Murphy remained hospitalised on Sunday after seeking medical care for numbness in his arm the day before, his chief-of-staff, Allison Herwitt, said in a statement.

She said he was “responding well to treatment” at John Hopkins, one of the country’s top hospitals.
“The doctors are encouraged by his progress, he is awake and alert, and we are optimistic he will make a full recovery,” Herwitt said.
Murphy is not up for re-election in Tuesday’s midterms that will decide which party controls Congress, but is considered a potential presidential candidate in 2028.

A 20-year senator from the state of Connecticut, Murphy serves as a top Democrat on two powerful Senate committees: appropriations, which decides how US government funds are allocated, and foreign relations.
Murphy toured the Middle East in October, the first regional trip by a US Democrat since the US-Israel war on Iran began in February.
He has been a fierce critic of US President Donald Trump and the Iran war, pledging that Democrats will withhold funding for the war if they win the Senate on Tuesday.

He accused the US Defense Department of denying him access to a US military base in Qatar during his trip last month and has pledged to investigate Trump and his family for alleged corruption if Democrats win the Senate.
Trump said he was “really surprised” to learn about Murphy’s stroke, adding that “nobody wants to have that”.

title_en: India's opposition holds mega rally seeking election chief's resignation
title_zh: 印度反对派将举行大型集会寻求选举主席辞职
summary: Thousands gathered in the heart of delhi, calling for the chief election commissioner to step down.
summary_zh: 此举正值选民名册修改活动引发越来越多的抗议，担心选民名册修改将导致 1.3 亿选民被剔除。
body_en: Tens of thousands gathered in Delhi for a rally demanding the resignation of India's chief election commissioner over a controversial revision of voter lists.

Organised by the opposition INDIA bloc and led by Rahul Gandhi's Congress party, the protest drew many of the alliance's most prominent leaders in a show of strength against Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government.
Protesters waved flags and chanted "Save the vote, save the country" and "Vote thief, give up power".

It was the latest in a series of protests over electoral roll revision that the opposition says has removed eligible voters to benefit the Bharatiya Janata Party. The BJP and the Election Commission deny the allegations.

The crowds gathered at Ramlila Maidan, a sprawling ground in central Delhi known for hosting major political and cultural events. Some protesters sang and danced to patriotic Bollywood songs, while others waited beneath a large canopy in the colours of the Indian flag to hear opposition leaders speak.
Gandhi and several senior opposition leaders arrived at the venue in an open jeep, travelling through crowds of cheering supporters.

The event was also attended by Congress leaders Sonia Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge, alongside leaders of regional parties such as Mamata Banerjee, Akhilesh Yadav, Mehbooba Mufti, Supriya Sule and Tejashwi Yadav.
Addressing the crowds, Rahul Gandhi said those gathered had sent a message to Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar .
"This is not the voice of a single political party or of politicians. It is the voice of India's youth, women, farmers and workers," he said.
"We will not allow democracy to be destroyed in India. We will not allow the constitution to be destroyed."

Other opposition leaders echoed Gandhi's criticism of the Election Commission. Congress president Kharge said the alliance would continue its campaign until Kumar resigned, while Banerjee pledged to keep fighting against what she described as threats to democracy.

Speaking to reporters in Delhi on Sunday, senior BJP leader and federal minister JP Nadda accused the opposition of trying to create unrest and destabilise the government under the guise of defending democracy.
He described the rally as a "calculated conspiracy to plunge the nation into anarchy - in the name of democracy".
At the centre of the dispute is an exercise known as the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), which has resulted in more than 130 million names being removed from India's draft electoral rolls.

The Election Commission says the exercise is intended to remove duplicate registrations and the names of people who have died, moved away or are otherwise ineligible to vote. It says eligible voters who have been wrongly excluded can seek to have their names restored.
But opposition parties allege that the process is removing legitimate voters and could benefit the governing BJP in future elections.

The controversy deepened in September when The Indian Express newspaper reported , external that Kumar had made key decisions about the revision despite repeated objections from the two other election commissioners.
The poll panel said differences of opinion were normal in any institution and did not affect its functioning.
Sunday's rally followed weeks of protests over the voter-list revision, including demonstrations by student groups and the Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP).
Last month, Gandhi led tens of thousands on a march from central Delhi's Connaught Place to the Supreme Court, demanding Kumar's resignation.
body_zh: 数万人聚集在德里举行集会，要求印度首席选举专员因对选民名单进行有争议的修改而辞职。
这次抗议活动由反对派印度集团组织，由拉胡尔·甘地领导的国大党领导，吸引了该联盟许多最著名的领导人，以展示反对总理纳伦德拉·莫迪政府的实力。
抗议者挥舞旗帜，高呼“拯救选票，拯救国家”和“选票贼，放弃权力”。
这是针对选举名册修改的一系列抗议活动中的最新一起，反对派称，选举名册修改已删除了符合资格的选民，以使印度人民党受益。印度人民党和选举委员会否认这些指控。
人群聚集在拉姆利拉迈丹，这是德里市中心的一片广阔土地，以举办重大政治和文化活动而闻名。一些抗议者随着宝莱坞的爱国歌曲载歌载舞，而另一些抗议者则在印度国旗颜色的大天篷下等待，聆听反对派领导人的讲话。
甘地和几位反对派高级领导人乘坐敞篷吉普车穿过欢呼的支持者人群抵达会场。
国大党领导人索尼娅·甘地和马利卡琼·哈尔格，以及玛玛塔·班纳吉、阿克希勒什·亚达夫、梅赫布巴·穆夫蒂、苏普里亚·苏莱和特贾什维·亚达夫等地区政党领导人也出席了此次活动。
拉胡尔·甘地向人群发表讲话说，聚集的人们已向莫迪、内政部长阿米特·沙阿和首席选举专员贾内什·库马尔发出了信息。
“这不是单一政党或政客的声音。这是印度青年、妇女、农民和工人的声音，”他说。
“我们不会允许印度的民主被摧毁。我们不会允许宪法被摧毁。”
其他反对派领导人也响应了甘地对选举委员会的批评。国大党主席哈格表示，该联盟将继续开展竞选活动，直至库马尔辞职，而班纳吉则承诺继续打击她所说的对民主的威胁。
印度人民党高级领导人兼联邦部长 JP Nadda 周日在德里对记者发表讲话，指责反对派试图以捍卫民主为幌子制造骚乱并破坏政府稳定。
他将这次集会描述为“一场精心策划的阴谋，旨在以民主的名义使国家陷入无政府状态”。
争议的核心是一项名为“特别强化修订”(SIR) 的行动，该行动已导致超过 1.3 亿人的名字从印度的选民名单中删除。
选举委员会表示，此举的目的是消除重复登记以及已死亡、搬走或因其他原因而无投票资格的人的姓名。它说，被错误排除在外的合格选民可以寻求恢复自己的名字。
但反对党声称，这一过程正在消除合法选民，并可能在未来的选举中使执政的印度人民党受益。
9 月份，《印度快报》对外报道称，尽管其他两名选举委员一再反对，但库马尔仍做出了有关修订的关键决定，争议进一步加深。
民意调查小组表示，意见分歧在任何机构都是正常的，不会影响其运作。
周日的集会是在针对选民名单修改进行了数周的抗议活动之后举行的，其中包括学生团体和 Z 世代领导的蟑螂党 (CJP) 的示威活动。
上个月，甘地率领数万人从德里市中心的康诺特广场游行至最高法院，要求库马尔辞职。

body_en: Turkey has been hit by powerful thunderstorms and a fatal tornado this week with more heavy rain expected

Heavy rain and strong winds will continue to affect parts of south-eastern Europe and Turkey over the next few days, as an area of low pressure in the region has allowed for the formation of powerful thunderstorms. During a particularly intense thunderstorm in Antalya, a coastal city in the south-west of Turkey, the formation of a tornado resulted in the deaths of four construction workers on Tuesday. Authorities in Greece and Turkey have released severe rainfall and flooding warnings, as a further 100-150mm (nearly 4-6in) of rain is expected this week in central Greece and western parts of Turkey, with locally higher totals possible.

Travelling eastwards towards south Asia, strong winds and heavy rainfall have swept across the Indian regions of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh as Cyclone Arnab made landfall. With wind gusts in excess of 85mph (140km/h) and rainfall totals in some regions exceeding 200mm, the severe storm has prompted mass evacuations of more than 180,000 people, as well as widespread disruption to energy and transport infrastructure. The cyclone will weaken as it continues to traverse northwards over the coming days, though will continue to deliver heavy rain to parts of northern and central India as it does so.
body_zh: 土耳其本周遭遇强烈雷暴和致命龙卷风袭击，预计还会有更多大雨
未来几天，大雨和强风将继续影响东南欧和土耳其的部分地区，因为该地区的低压区域导致了强大的雷暴的形成。周二，土耳其西南部沿海城市安塔利亚遭遇特别强烈的雷暴，龙卷风的形成导致四名建筑工人死亡。希腊和土耳其当局已发布严重降雨和洪水警告，预计希腊中部和土耳其西部地区本周将进一步降雨 100-150 毫米（近 4-6 英寸），局部地区降雨总量可能更高。
随着气旋“阿纳布”登陆，向东向南亚移动，强风和强降雨席卷了印度奥里萨邦和安得拉邦地区。阵风超过 85 英里/小时（140 公里/小时），部分地区降雨量超过 200 毫米，这场严重风暴已导致超过 18 万人大规模疏散，能源和交通基础设施也受到广泛破坏。未来几天，气旋将继续向北移动，强度将减弱，但仍将给印度北部和中部部分地区带来大雨。
